name: APAR: Auto-Parallel Auto-Regressive Decoding
executive_summary: Instruct-tune the model itself to recognize parallelizable structure in its own output and spawn multiple generation threads directly, instead of relying on an external skeleton-then-expand prompting template.
description: A direct successor to Skeleton-of-Thought's goal (reduce latency by generating independent parts of an answer in parallel), but moves the mechanism from the prompt into the model: instruct-tuning on data containing hierarchical/parallelizable structures teaches the model to autonomously plan its own generation and emit control tokens that spawn parallel generation threads, rather than requiring a separate skeleton-generation prompting stage. Reports up to 2x speed-up alone, and up to 4x when combined with speculative decoding. Unlike Skeleton-of-Thought, this is a training-time technique, not something achievable through prompting an off-the-shelf model — included here as the training-time complement so the parallel-decoding lineage in this catalog is complete.
when_to_use: You control model fine-tuning and want parallel-generation speed-ups without a separate skeleton-prompting stage or the coordination overhead of managing parallel API calls yourself.
when_not_to_use: Working with a fixed, already-trained model with no fine-tuning access — use Skeleton-of-Thought's prompting-only approach instead.
known_pitfalls: Requires instruct-tuning infrastructure and training data with hierarchical/parallelizable structure; not a pure prompting-layer technique, so it doesn't transfer to models you can't fine-tune.

primary_source.authors: Liu, Zeng, Wang, Zhang, Tang, Dong
primary_source.title: APAR: LLMs Can Do Auto-Parallel Auto-Regressive Decoding
